summary: RBAC end-to-end validated. Backend: 13/13 pytest passing on /app/backend/tests/test_rbac.py (permission matrix, dual accounts, review workflow, risk override, audit, hierarchy). Frontend: internal login redirects to /admin, external redirects to /panel, superadmin sees all 8 sidebar sections and can open user edit dialog, review tabs and audit page. One UI bug found: Finanzas sees 'Usuarios' in sidebar (should be hidden per spec).

ui_bugs.issue: Sidebar 'Usuarios' entry uses perm 'consultar' — every internal role sees it. Requirement says Finanzas (and other roles without administrar_usuarios) should NOT see Usuarios. Change NAV entry Usuarios to perm 'administrar_usuarios' so only superadmin/admin_general see it.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.js change the Usuarios NAV item perm from 'consultar' to 'administrar_usuarios' so Finanzas/Revisión/Soporte/etc. don't see it. AdminUsers page itself already guards write actions with canManage.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1057 lines — consider splitting admin/RBAC endpoints into /app/backend/routers/admin.py for maintainability.
admin_review_property uses get_current_user + manual has_perm checks instead of the require_permission dependency (works but inconsistent).
Seeded internal staff users never get their password refreshed if Interno123! changes (idempotent-with-password-refresh recommended).
GET /api/admin/documents exposes tenant_name + monthly_income of ALL applications to anyone with consultar_documentos_sensibles — consider pagination/filtering to reduce exposure.

can_grant() defaults actor_rank to 1 for unranked roles; only superadmin=3 and admin_general=2 are ranked — other internal roles (soporte/finanzas/etc.) implicitly get rank 1 which is fine because they lack administrar_usuarios.
External accounts are truly dual: POST /api/properties by an arrendatario succeeds, PATCH /users/me role toggles the active profile — confirmed working.

rca of the issue: Bug RCA — Sidebar over-permissive: In AdminLayout.js the NAV array grants Usuarios visibility to anyone with 'consultar' permission (all internal roles). Since 'administrar_usuarios' is only held by superadmin/admin_general, and the spec says only they should see Usuarios, the NAV entry must use perm:'administrar_usuarios'. Reproduction: login as finanzas@rentalo.mx / Interno123! → /admin sidebar shows 'Usuarios'. Fix: one-line change in AdminLayout.js NAV constant.
